title: Strategic Foresight – Canada's Industrial Resilience
description: The Department of Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada has a requirement for strategic foresight research and analysis to assess the impacts of emerging geopolitical, economic and technological developments on Canada's industrial competitiveness, manufacturing resilience and digital opportunities. The work will include developing and analyzing 12 to 16 potential future scenarios across four strategic contexts, examining their potential implications for Canada's industrial economy, supply chain resilience, trade relationships, technology ecosystems and government investment decisions. The Contractor will be required to facilitate working sessions and workshops with ISED representatives and senior management, prepare analytical materials, and deliver comprehensive foresight reports outlining key risks, opportunities, policy and investment considerations, and recommendations to support Canada's industrial policy and investment planning.

title: CHL NBC VE 4754 Pathologie mit Kühlzellen
description: Das Klinikum Centre Hospitalier de Luxembourg beabsichtigt im Zuge des Neubaus einige Pathologieeinrichtung gemäß dem Vergabeverfahren „Buch II Offenes Verfahren (Loi, Art. 63 und 65)" zu beschaffen. Bestandteil der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung und Montage von - 1 Leichenkühlzellenanlage mit Einzelfächern für 21 Verstorbenen (davon 3 Plätze adipöse) - 1 Leichenkühlzellenanlage für 1 radioaktive Verstorbenen - 18 Leichenmulde Standardgröße - 3 Leichenmulde Adipositas-Größe - 1 Leichenmulde Standardgröße für radioaktive Verstorbene - 1 Wasch- und Seziertisch fahrbar mit Schnittstelle Andockstation - 1 Andocksäule für fahrbaren Seziertisch - 1 Seziertisch, fahrbar für die Entnahme der Hornhäute - 1 Scherenwagen für Sargtransport - 3 Hydraulischer Leichenmulden-Hubwagen für Standardgröße und adipöse Verstorbene - 1 Katafalkrahmen, fahrbar, mit Kühlung inkl. Behang und Mulde - 1 Gefriertruhe für Körperteile mit Temperaturüberwachung - 2 Standleuchter (Elektrokerzen) Die Lieferung und Montage der Bestandteile soll nach dem folgenden Prioritäten-Schema getrennt ablaufen: Montage Unterkonstruktionen, Montage Leichenkühlzellanlagen, Lieferung Zubehör unmittelbar vor Inbetriebnahme (Diebstahlprävention). 1 Haupt- und 1 Nachbesserungstermin sind mit dem Angebotspreis abgegolten, wobei die Teilleistungen gemäß Terminplan gestaffelt einzutakten und mit der örtlichen Bauleitung/Fachbauleitung abzustimmen sind. Die gesetzliche Verjährungsfrist der Gewährleistungsansprüche beginnt mit der Abnahme der Leistung. Der Tag der Abnahme (komplette Montage inklusive Mängelbeseitigungen) ist der Gewährleistungsbeginn. Folgende Leistungen sind neben den gerätebezogenen Leistungen anzubieten und zu kalkulieren: - Bei der Kollisionsprüfung durch den koordinierenden Architekten (4Bund) ist durch den Auftragnehmer (AN) mitzuwirken. Die Montagepläne sind bei Erfordernis anzupassen. - Für Organisationsbesprechungen - auch teil- und abschnittsweise - hat der AN einen mit der Anlage in allen Teilen technisch und betrieblich vertrauten, sachkundigen Mitarbeiter beizustellen. - Weitere Leitungen gemäß den zusätzlichen technischen Vorbemerkungen der Medizintechnik. Eignungskriterien gemäß allgemeinen und besonderen Vertragsbedingungen, Punkt 1.10 / Punkt 2.10 Für die Lieferungen und Montagen der Geräte sind folgende Termine maßgebend: Möglicher Beginn Einbau: 24.09.2027 Spätester Abschluss Montagen: 29.03.2029 (Innenausbau + Technik gem. Generalablaufplan_V5) Unter Berücksichtigung des Starttermins ist ein Montageterminplan vorzulegen und ggf. an Vorgaben des Architekten (4Bund) anzupassen. Die jeweils für die Einbringung und Montage benötigten Zeiten sind pro Gerät zu hinterlegen.

title: Finland – Document creation, drawing, imaging, scheduling and productivity software package – Adoben käyttöoikeuksien jakelu- ja hallintapalvelu
description: Hankinnan kohteena on Adoben käyttöoikeuksien jakelu- ja hallintapalvelu solmittavan hankintasopimuksen mukaisesti. Jakelu- ja hallintapalvelussa Toimittaja tarjoaa Adoben ohjelmistotuotteiden jakelukanavat ja sopimuksen mukaiset muut palvelut Tilaajalle perustuen Tilaajan ja tämän Asiakkaiden käyttämiin osto-ohjelmiin. Käytössä ovat hallinnon- ja sivistyspuolen VIP Marketplace- osto-ohjelmat (GOV ja EDU). Tilaajalla on oikeus valita ja vaihtaa osto-ohjelmaa sopimuskaudella, mikäli se nähdään tarpeelliseksi. Toimittaja sitoutuu jälleenmyymään käyttöoikeuksia Tilaajan valitsemilla osto-ohjelmilla, joista voidaan sopia sopimuksen voimassaoloaikana siten, että osto-ohjelma alkaa ennen sopimuksen päättymistä. Toimittajalta vaaditaan vähintään Gold Certified Reseller -status sekä oikeus jälleenmyydä tuotteita GOV- ja EDU -asiakasryhmille. Tilaajalla on tällä hetkellä käytössä Adoben VIP Marketplace -osto-ohjelmaan kuuluvia ohjelmistolisenssejä, joten erikoisosaaminen VIP Marketplace osto-ohjelmasta on myös hankinnan kohteeseen liittyvä perusvaatimus. Käyttöoikeuksien vuosipäivä on hallintopuolen osalta 17.3.2027 ja EDU-puolen osalta 7.6.2027. Tarjouskilpailun perusteella valitaan yksi (1) sopimuskumppani, jonka kanssa sopimus solmitaan. Kiinteä sopimuskausi on voimassa kolme (3) vuotta, minkä jälkeen sopimus voi jatkua toistaiseksi voimassaolevana sovituin irtisanomisehdoin.

title: Parachute Packing Press
description: UPDATED/CORRECTED: This effort is for the procurement of (1) Parachute Packing Press Model GSU-449/E (PN: COM00150-1; NSN: 1670-99-555-6604) for the F/A-18 Kuwait Classic program. Under authority 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1) and implemented in FAR 6.302-l(b)(l), to try to develop this �asset" would incur costs that are not expected to be recouped through competition. Any attempt to procure a different part number would require the Government to fund a Preliminary Design Review (PDR) Critical Design Review (CDR) First Article Test (FAT) and Test & Evaluation (T&E) effort for a new vendor. The Government would have to fund personnel to be on the Source Selection Team to review proposals. Any change in form, fit or function would require changes to the existing Integrated Logistics Support (ILS) (technical publications, spares inventory, calibration) which would incur additional costs for update in the amount of $100,000 to $150,000. The process required to obtain an alternate asset is cost-prohibitive and would force the FMS Partner to utilize an asset that is not supported, compatible or interchangeable with the USN-approved configuration. Hence, the FMS partner would forfeit the fundamental benefits granted per the signed Letter of Acceptance (LOA). This requirement will be processed under the authority 10 U.S.C.2304(c)(1), only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Market Research was performed by the Lakehurst Technical team. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of this item is Martin Baker, CAGE: U1604. The CONUS branch of Martin Baker (1Q842) does not supply this item within the states. Martin Baker has only two authorized distributors, Allied Defense Industries, CAGE: 0GD25 and Integrated Procurement Technologies, CAGE: 4K0V2/05ZJ1. Martin Baker owns all of the proprietary rights to the engineering data and detailed product drawings. No additional vendors were identified through market research. As such, we recommend a limited competition, firm-fixed price procurement between the OEM Martin Baker and their authorized distributors, Allied Defense Industries, CAGE: 0GD25 and Integrated Procurement Technologies, CAGE: 4K0V2/05ZJ1.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Generalsanierung mit Erweiterung Inklusionskindergarten in Lappersdorf. Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8, gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1.
description: Der Markt Lappersdorf plant, den vorhandenen Inklusionskindergarten KGL mit 4 Kindergartengruppen zu sanieren und auf 7 Gruppen zu erweitern. Die Programmfläche beträgt insgesamt ca. 1600 qm. Der bestehende eingeschossige Kindergarten aus dem Baujahr 1970 an der Pielmühler Strasse wurde bereits mehrfach umgebaut und im Jahr 1990 erweitert. Der verputzte Mauerwerksbau hat Satteldächer mit unterschiedlichen Deckungen aus Zinkblech, Ziegel sowie teilweise mit einer PV-Anlage. Der Zustand des Kindergartens entspricht funktional nicht mehr dem Stand der Technik und muss saniert werden. Das Gebäude ist insbesondere energetisch und in Bezug auf Brandschutz sowie die Barrierefreiheit veraltet und muss entsprechend ertüchtigt werden. Für die geplante Generalsanierung und Erweiterung wurden die Leistungsphasen 1 - 3 bereits erbracht. Die Baugenehmigung ist beantragt. Das vorliegende VgV-Vergabeverfahren ist Grundlage für die Vergabe der Architektenleistungen der Ausführungsplanung, Vorbereitung und Mitwirkung bei der Vergabe und Objektüberwachung, also der Leistunsphasen 5 bis 8 gem. HOAI. Da eine Bewerbung des vorbefassten Büros nicht ausgeschlossen werden kann, werden zum Ausgleich des Informationsvorsprungs diverse Informationsunterlagen zur Verfügung gestellt, u.a. Planungsgrundlagen, Entwurfsplanung und Kosten. Für die Entwurfsplanung liegt das Nutzungsrecht am Urheberrecht beim Markt Lappersdorf. Die bestehenden 4 Kindergartengruppen sind während der Bauzeit ausgelagert und werden provisorisch in Containern auf dem naheliegenden Rathausparkplatz untergebracht. Die Auslagerung ist nicht Gegenstand des Auftrags. Die Außenanlagen des bestehenden Kindergartens werden während der Bauphase weiter als Freianlagen zum Spielen genutzt. Gegenstand des Auftrags sind die Architektenleistungen der Objektplanung Gebäude und Innenräume gem. HOAI Teil 3 Abschnitt 1, Leistungsphasen 5 bis 8. Der Auftraggeber rechnet für die Kostengruppen 300 und 400 mit Kosten von ca. 6,2 Mio. Euro einschl. Mehrwertsteuer und ordnet die Maßnahme der Honorarzone III zu. Eine Vergabe der Leistungen in Stufen wird vorbehalten. Aus der stufenweisen Beauftragung können keine zusätzlichen Honoraransprüche geltend gemacht werden. Die Planungen sind unmittelbar nach Auftragsvergabe zu beginnen. Voraussichtlich werden folgende Förderprogramme in Anspruch genommen: FAG-Förderung und KfW-Förderung. Betreiber des Kindergartens ist die Katholische Jugendfürsorge der Diözese Regensburg e.V.

title: CAWT PEACEPLUS EASY Project: Early Intervention Support for Children, Young People and Families presenting with Neurodevelopmental Needs (SHSCT Area)
description: This is a project supported by PEACEPLUS, a programme managed by the Special EU Programmes Body (SEUPB). The CAWT PEACEPLUS Early Intervention Support Youth Hubs (EASY) project aims to establish new cross border early intervention support services for families with children and young people presenting with traits consistent with a neurodevelopmental type need or who have been recently diagnosed with a neurodevelopmental condition. By providing help based on presenting need/symptoms, the project aims to improve outcomes for children, young people and their families by helping families' access appropriate support, based on needs at the right time and in the right place. This procurement exercise and the subsequent service to be commissioned will cover only the Northern Ireland delivery area, which is located within the boundaries of the Southern Health and Social Care Trust (SHSCT). Please refer to the full suite of tender documents for further information on the service requirements. title: Medically Managed Intensive Residential Withdrawal Management (IIWM) Services
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Medically Managed Intensive Residential Withdrawal Management (IIWM) Services The Court Services and Offender Supervision Agency (CSOSA) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing Medically Managed Intensive Residential Withdrawal Management (IIWM) services for individuals referred by CSOSA. The Government seeks information regarding industry capability, facility capacity, clinical and medical staffing, licensing and accreditation, geographic availability, transportation, transition planning, performance measurement, and potential pricing approaches. The anticipated acquisition would include one 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods, for a potential total period of performance of 60 months. Responses will help CSOSA assess the availability of responsible sources, consider an appropriate acquisition strategy, refine performance requirements, and determine whether a small-business set-aside or another socioeconomic strategy is suitable.

DLA Energy Bulk Petroleum Services Business unite-FESBA seeks to identify potential qualified businesses that are able to perform the required tasks to include fuel operations, management and administrative actions pertaining to the receipt, storage and handling, quality assurance/surveillance, inventory management, accounting, and issue/sales of DLA Energy fuel products to authorized DoD customers. The Contractor must be able to furnish all personnel, vehicles, equipment, supplies, and/or expendable materials necessary for providing these services (unless otherwise stipulated) at Incirlik, Turkey. Interested companies should respond to the questions below. Any information provided to the Government as a result of this notice is voluntary. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this notice. All responses to this notice are to be submitted by 1100 hours local time Ft Belvoir, VA on December 3, 2026. Only responses submitted via E-Mail will be considered. E-Mail submissions shall be sent to Jafari Townsell at Jafari.1.Townsell@dla.mil and CC Mark Laskoski at Mark.Laskoski@dla.mil The Government plans to award a firm-fixed price contract for a four-year base period, one fiveyear option period, and six one-month options to extend. In response to this notice please provide the following: 1. A company profile to include number employees, office location(s), DUNS/CAGE Code number, and a statement regarding current business status. Please note that registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) is required for DLA Energy contractors. 2. Capability of providing qualified and experienced personnel, with appropriate clearances, if required. 3. Past Performance: Do you have past performance as a prime contractor or subcontractor on service contract for similar fuels management requirements? If your firm acted as subcontractor or joint venture, name the prime contractor or other party, the specific work performed and percentage. Address any past performance problems (if any), and resolutions taken. 4. Do you anticipate any type of teaming arrangement for this requirement? If yes, please address what kind of arrangement and what percentage of work, type (s) of service would you perform. 5. Does your company have the financial capability and financial stability, and/or adequate lines of credit to sustain and support a five-year contract with multiple locations, in the event there are delays with the payment process? 6. What realistic phase-in period would you require to commence performance with personnel, equipment, and materials? title: Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting- Sources Sought Notice / Request for Information
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Water Treatment Chemicals, Testing, Monitoring, and Reporting BPA Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Notice Type Sources Sought / Request for Information / Market Research Agency Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) Contracting Office Federal Bureau of Prisons, Facilities Management Branch 320 First Street NW Washington, DC 20534 Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued solely for market research purposes in accordance with FAR Part 10. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is seeking qualified contractors capable of providing water treatment chemicals, water testing, treatment recommendations, reporting, and related support services for federal correctional institutions nationwide, under a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA). This notice is not a solicitation and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract or BPA. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with responding to this notice. The contractor shall furnish all personnel, chemicals, testing equipment, laboratory services, transportation, reporting systems, technical support, and related resources necessary to support boiler water systems, chiller water loops, cooling towers, and domestic water systems at participating BOP facilities. Services include water sampling and analysis, chemical treatment programs, Legionella testing, domestic water testing, water quality reporting, corrective action recommendations, trend analysis, regulatory compliance support, and maintenance of a secure online reporting portal. Contractors shall provide monthly and quarterly reports and maintain water quality treatment programs designed to reduce corrosion, scaling, biological growth, and other operational risks associated with institutional water systems. The requirement includes support for multiple BOP institutions located throughout the United States. Contractors should carefully consider the geographic distribution of performance locations and demonstrate their ability to provide timely service, technical support, testing, and delivery of treatment chemicals to institutions nationwide. Respondents shall identify any planned subcontracting arrangements and provide examples of water treatment, water testing, boiler treatment, cooling tower treatment, Legionella monitoring, or similar services performed directly by their organization as the prime contractor. Experience performed solely by subcontractors or teaming partners should be separately identified. Any future small business set-aside acquisition resulting from this requirement will be subject to the applicable limitations on subcontracting requirements contained in FAR 52.219-14 and 13 CFR �125.6. Respondents should describe how they would comply with these requirements if awarded a contract. Vendors should carefully review the draft requirements before submitting a response. The Government is seeking capability information from firms that can directly perform and support the full scope of services, including water testing, chemical treatment, reporting, and compliance support across multiple correctional institutions. Responses that do not address the firm's ability to meet the requirements outlined herein may be considered less useful for market research purposes. Information contained within the draft Statement of Work serves as the basis for this market research effort. Scope of Requirements The Government is interested in determining industry capability to provide the following services: 1. Water Treatment Chemicals Provide water treatment chemicals and related application support for: Boiler systems Chiller water loops Cooling towers Domestic water systems The contractor must be capable of supporting multiple geographically dispersed correctional institutions. 2. Boiler Water Testing and Treatment Provide: Monthly testing of boiler water systems Written treatment reports Corrective recommendations Chemical treatment programs Corrosion prevention measures Contractors must be capable of implementing treatment recommendations and supplying required chemicals within fifteen (15) calendar days of test results. 3. Chiller Loop and Cooling Tower Testing Provide: Monthly seasonal testing Water quality analysis Treatment recommendations Corrosion prevention services Cooling tower chemical treatment Contractors must provide solutions to maintain water quality and system efficiency. 4. Domestic Water and Legionella Testing Provide quarterly testing at active inmate housing institutions, including: Legionella E. coli Lead Arsenic Nitrates PFAS pH Mineral content Contractors shall identify deficiencies and provide corrective recommendations. 5. Online Reporting Platform Provide and maintain a secure web-based platform capable of: Institution-level user access Regional and Central Office oversight access Monthly and quarterly report storage Historical trending analysis Water quality dashboards Chemical usage tracking Compliance reporting Corrective action tracking The platform should support enterprise-wide visibility across all participating institutions. Anticipated NAICS Code The Government is considering the following NAICS codes and seeks industry feedback regarding the most appropriate code: NAICS Description 325998 All Other Miscellaneous Chemical Product and Preparation Manufacturing 541380 Testing Laboratories and Services 561210 Facilities Support Services 221310 Water Supply and Irrigation Systems Respondents are encouraged to recommend alternative NAICS codes if more appropriate. The Government may use information received in response to this notice for acquisition planning purposes only. Participation in this market research effort is not a prerequisite for participation in any future solicitation. title: Ireland – Construction work – National Centre for Research and Remembrance | Phase 3-B Main Works | Main Contractor and Project Supervisor Construction Stage (PSCS)
description: The Phase 3B Main Works development will consist of: a. The change of use of the former Our Lady of Charity and Refuge Convent and Magdalene Laundry to the National Centre for Research and Remembrance (NCRR) (total circa 7510sqm); the provision of a purpose built archival repository (circa 4,030sqm, 2-4 storeys over basement); the provision of 3 storey entrance wing (circa 210sqm) accessed via new shared pedestrian and vehicular entrances from Seán MacDermott Street Lower and Railway Street; and the conservation, refurbishment, and upgrade of the existing convent, chapel and dormitory block (circa 3,490sqm). The development will also include provision of dedicated garden with hard and soft landscaping as a Garden of Reflection (circa 430sqm) and provision of surface bicycle parking; hard and soft landscaping; integrated ESB substation; and all associated site works. The building will include document repositories at basement level, exhibition spaces, conservation laboratories, consultation rooms and a public reading room, offices and meeting rooms. b. The provision of a new Educational Facility (circa 3,690sqm) 3-5 storey block over basement (with rooftop terrace and rooftop plantroom enclosure setback at 3rd and 5th floors respectively). This building will be located to the South West end of the main site (Site A) facing onto Railway Street and accessed via shared new entrance from Railway Street; and will be provided with surface bicycle parking and 3no. bicycle shelters; hard and soft landscaping; a new external courtyard; and all associated site works. The building will include classrooms, workshops, offices and meeting rooms. c. The conservation and refurbishment of the existing derelict 2 storey Dispensary Building to provide a Community based Family and Parenting Support Facility (circa 480sqm); the addition of a new 2 storey extension (circa 275sqm,, total circa 760sqm) to the North side with glazed entrance link accessed from within the NCRR development site; the provision of surface bicycle parking; external bin enclosure; hard and soft landscaping to a new external play space; and all associated site works. The building will include teaching, workshop and play spaces, offices and meeting rooms. d. The provision of a Community based Family and Parenting Support Facility attached to the existing Scots Church (Site B), and to adjoining site 61 Seán MacDermott Street Lower, Dublin 1; the development will include the removal of the existing 2 storey façade; the conservation of the historic Scots Church façade (a protected structure RPS:7480); the provision of new 2 storey extension (circa 435sqm) with rooftop plantroom enclosure setback; a new external play space; and all associated site works.

title: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Regulated Medical Waste
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity intends to award a sole-source Firm Fixed Price commercial services bridge contract to the incumbent contractor, Advant-Edge Solutions of Middle Atlantic, Inc. under the authority of 10 USC 3204(a)(1) and RFO sections 6.103-1(b), 6.103-1(c)(2)(i) and 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), on the basis that the continued provision of these highly specialized medical waste disposal services is available from only one responsible source for the required bridge period, and that a change in source for a short-term bridge contract would result in substantial duplication of transition costs to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. The proposed bridge contract will provide continued enterprise Regulated Medical Waste (RMW) collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, manifesting, reporting, and related services for all military medical treatment facilities (including the U.S. Military Entrance Processing Command�s (USMEPCOM�s), Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS), and the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES)) in all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico. The anticipated bridge period of performance is February 1, 2027, through July 31, 2027, with one optional period from August 1, 2027 to 31 January 2028. The bridge contract is necessary to maintain uninterrupted RMW services while the Government completes the competitive follow-on procurement, which is currently in active source selection, and transitions services to the follow-on contractor. The current contract expires on January 31, 2027. While the Government is actively completing the competitive follow-on procurement, conducting a separate competitive acquisition for a short-term bridge contract requires approximately 90 to 120 calendar days of combined acquisition and transition lead time. The Government cannot complete a separate competitive bridge acquisition and physical transition prior to January 31, 2027, without creating an unacceptable risk of a lapse in mission-critical RMW services. In addition, the Government would not recover the duplicated transition and onboarding costs of switching contractors twice within a three-to-six-month window. Accordingly, interested sources that believe they can satisfy the entire enterprise requirement for this short-term bridge period must demonstrate their ability to execute an accelerated transition and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, without interruption to RMW services at all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico locations. Capability statements must describe the source�s proposed transition approach; available staffing, collection containers, transportation assets, treatment and disposal capacity; required permits and licenses; site onboarding process; and measures to mitigate service-continuity risks during the compressed transition period. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract (nor will the Government reimburse any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice). However, interested sources that believe they can meet the full requirement and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, may submit a capability statement to Mr. Luke Burke at luke.e.burke.civ@health.mil POC no later than 2:30 p.m. Eastern Time on December 2, 2026. The Government will evaluate timely capability statements solely to determine whether a responsible source can meet the Government�s requirements within the required timeframe.

title: Y1DA--FY27 NRM - EHRM Base 509-22-701 - EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades - Downtown Division - Construction (VA-27-00011175)
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project for the Charlie Norwood VA Medical Center located in Augusta, GA. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Charlie Norwood VAMC is seeking a general contractor to furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and supervision and perform all work necessary to complete the EHRM Infrastructure Upgrades Construction project. Work includes, but is not limited to, Verify existing conditions prior to commencing work. Coordinate all construction activities with the VA, COR, facility operations, affected services, and other contractors. Protect existing VA facilities, equipment, utilities, infrastructure, patients, staff, and visitors. Maintain required hospital operations and access throughout construction. Provide required infection control, interim life safety, utility shutdown, fire protection, environmental, and safety measures. Coordinate work involving existing electrical, mechanical, telecommunications, information technology, fire alarm, security, and other facility systems. Obtain required approvals before performing work that affects existing VA operations or utility systems. Provide temporary services and protection necessary to maintain facility operations. Perform testing, inspection, startup, commissioning, and verification of installed systems as required by the contract documents. Correct deficiencies identified during inspections, testing, commissioning, and final acceptance. Provide complete as-built documentation and operation and maintenance information as required. as required to complete the scope of this project. All work is to be performed in accordance with the drawings and specifications. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued either as a Request For Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR Part 14, considering Price only. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in mid to late-December 2026. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000.00 and $50,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 (size standard $45.0 million) applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAAR Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Provide specific examples that relate aspects of previous projects to the proposed project. Describe specific technical skills and key personnel your company possess to perform the requirements described under description of work. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. Section 6: Project Labor Agreement (PLA) - A PLA is defined as a pre-hire Collective Bargaining Agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement described in 29 U.S.C. 158(f). title: Remove and Install Dorm Furniture (Commodity)
description: The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and other items necessary to perform all work required for the purchase, delivery, uncrating, and full setup of dormitory furniture at a designated dormitory facility located at Francis E. Warren AFB, Wyoming. In addition to delivering and installing the new furniture, the contractor shall be responsible for the complete removal, palletizing, and banding of existing dormitory furniture sets, which must be safely transported and staged in the dormitory courtyard for Government disposition. All freight and shipping must be provided under FOB Destination terms directly to Francis E. Warren AFB. The specific items, finishes, and quantities anticipated under this requirement are as follows: forty-eight (48) each Twin XL single beds equipped with locking bed springs, ninety-six (96) each two-drawer underbed stackable storage units, forty-eight (48) each two-drawer nightstands, forty-eight (48) each one-drawer study desks, and twelve (12) each common-area coffee tables, all manufactured in a uniform Cherry Oak finish. Accompanying seating requirements include forty-eight (48) each desk chairs featuring Cherry Oak construction with blue upholstered seat cushions, and forty-eight (48) each recliner lounge chairs in blue upholstery. The contractor shall provide freight charges for one (1) each shipment to FOB Destination to F.E. Warren AFB, Wyoming. The contractor shall also provide a setup and installation fee for one (1) complete job. Lastly, the contractor shall provide a removal, palletizing, and banding fee for one (1) complete job.

title: INVITATION TO SUBMIT AN EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (EOI) – Office space
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is asking interested parties to provide information for a potential lease of space that meets the following criteria: Section A: Lease Components • a lease term of approximately 10 years, commencing on or about May 1, 2030, with a right of early termination anytime on or after May 1, 2038 provided written notice is given at least 12 months prior, plus an option to extend the lease for One (1) additional period of Two (2) years; • approximately 4,281 usable square metres (um2) of office space, and one (1) parking space; • the proposed space must be available approximately 65 weeks prior to the above-noted lease commencement date so all space(s) may be prepared for occupancy; • the proposed space should satisfy or be capable of satisfying the following criteria: 1. the proposed space should be within an office or commercial building; industrial type buildings and those with industrial space will not be considered. A mixed use building may be considered at the sole discretion of PSPC; 2. preference may be given to spaces with any or all of the following: a highly visible storefront space, on a main road, with direct pedestrian access from the street; 3. a minimum of 771 um2 of the proposed space must be located on a floor with public access; preference may be given to spaces located on the main floor; 4. the proposed space must be contiguous within each floor; 5. if the proposed space is offered on multiple floors, consecutive floors are preferred; 6. a dedicated telecommunication room measuring no less than 20.3 um² within the proposed space must be provided; this area will not form part of the Lessee’s usable area noted above but will be included in the rentable area calculation; 7. cleaning services will be required during business hours; 8. the proposed space must be fully accessible to persons with a disability; 9. parking for approximately 25 vehicles must be available to the public within a one (1) block radius of the proposed space; 10. a public transit stop must be within 600 metres of the buildings main entrance, and the frequency of service must not be greater than 30 minute intervals between the hours of 0700 hours and 1800 hours, Monday to Friday inclusive and there must be an accessible walking route between the public transit stop and the building; 11. acceptable space for the installation of bicycle rack(s); 12. the physical characteristics of the lands and the building and the area and environment surrounding it, including neighbouring land uses, shall be compatible with the Lessee’s intended use of the accommodation; 13. the dimensions of the proposed space must be compatible for efficient design and use; • the proposed space must be located in the city of Edmonton and within the following boundaries (the geographical boundaries include sites on either side of the roads): North: Whitemud Drive NW to 91 Street NW / 91 Street NW to Roper Road NW / Roper Road NW to 34 Street NW East: 34th Street NW South: Ellerslie Road SW West: 170th Street SW / Terwillegar Drive NW In the event of any discrepancy between the attached map and text description of the geographic boundaries, the text description shall prevail. This map is to be used for presentation purposes only and is not a legal document • on or before the lease commencement date, the proposed space will have to comply with all requirements contained in PSPC’s Standards for Leased Accommodation, a copy of which may be obtained from the contact listed in Section F; Note: PSPC may wish to visit or inspect the proposed space upon reasonable notice and a threat and risk assessment may be undertaken in order to assess potential threats to the security of the proposed space and to the public.

title: Defense Health Agency (DHA) Regulated Medical Waste
description: The Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity intends to award a sole-source Firm Fixed Price commercial services bridge contract to the incumbent contractor, Advant-Edge Solutions of Middle Atlantic, Inc. under the authority of 10 USC 3204(a)(1) and RFO sections 6.103-1(b), 6.103-1(c)(2)(i) and 6.103-1(c)(2)(ii), on the basis that the continued provision of these highly specialized medical waste disposal services is available from only one responsible source for the required bridge period, and that a change in source for a short-term bridge contract would result in substantial duplication of transition costs to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition and unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency�s requirements. The proposed bridge contract will provide continued enterprise Regulated Medical Waste (RMW) collection, transportation, treatment, disposal, manifesting, reporting, and related services for all military medical treatment facilities (including the U.S. Military Entrance Processing Command�s (USMEPCOM�s), Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS), and the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES)) in all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico. The anticipated bridge period of performance is February 1, 2027, through July 31, 2027, with one optional period from August 1, 2027 to 31 January 2028. The bridge contract is necessary to maintain uninterrupted RMW services while the Government completes the competitive follow-on procurement, which is currently in active source selection, and transitions services to the follow-on contractor. The current contract expires on January 31, 2027. While the Government is actively completing the competitive follow-on procurement, conducting a separate competitive acquisition for a short-term bridge contract requires approximately 90 to 120 calendar days of combined acquisition and transition lead time. The Government cannot complete a separate competitive bridge acquisition and physical transition prior to January 31, 2027, without creating an unacceptable risk of a lapse in mission-critical RMW services. In addition, the Government would not recover the duplicated transition and onboarding costs of switching contractors twice within a three-to-six-month window. Accordingly, interested sources that believe they can satisfy the entire enterprise requirement for this short-term bridge period must demonstrate their ability to execute an accelerated transition and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, without interruption to RMW services at all fifty (50) United States, Guam, and Puerto Rico locations. Capability statements must describe the source�s proposed transition approach; available staffing, collection containers, transportation assets, treatment and disposal capacity; required permits and licenses; site onboarding process; and measures to mitigate service-continuity risks during the compressed transition period. This notice is not a request for competitive proposals and does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award a contract (nor will the Government reimburse any costs incurred in preparing a response to this notice). However, interested sources that believe they can meet the full requirement and commence full performance on February 1, 2027, may submit a capability statement to Mr. Luke Burke at luke.e.burke.civ@health.mil POC no later than 1:00 p.m. Eastern Time on December 3, 2026. The Government will evaluate timely capability statements solely to determine whether a responsible source can meet the Government�s requirements within the required timeframe.

title: Y1DZ--673-901 Brooksville CBOC Renovation Minor Design-Build - Brooksville, FL
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: This Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The VA Office of Facilities Acquisition (OFA), Program Contracting Activity Center (PCAC) is conducting a market research to identify qualified sources capable of performing a Design-Build (DB) project. Services to include Architect and Engineering (DB A/E) design services, site preparation and DB Construction (DB C) services for the renovation of the Brooksville Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) at the Brooksville VA Clinic located at 14540 Cortez Boulevard, Suite 108, Brooksville, Florida 34613-6001. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veterans Affairs has a requirement for a Design-Build renovation of the Brooksville Community-Based Outpatient Clinic (CBOC) under Project No. 673-901. The project includes completion of the remaining design effort, validation of existing conditions, preparation of final construction documents, and execution of construction activities necessary to renovate and modernize the facility in accordance with current VA standards, life safety requirements, operational needs, and applicable VA criteria. This Design-Build project includes all necessary architectural, engineering, specialty consulting, commissioning, and construction services required to deliver a complete and operational renovation. The scope includes review and incorporation of prior design documents, infrastructure upgrades to HVAC and electrical systems, OI&T/telecommunications improvements, safety and security enhancements, fire protection improvements, building envelope repairs, roof and water intrusion remediation, and all associated architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, low-voltage, civil, and site-related work. The contractor shall perform comprehensive site investigation and field verification of existing conditions and develop detailed phasing, infection control, containment, and construction logistics plans to support continued operation of the clinic during construction. Work shall be coordinated with facility stakeholders to maintain safe access for patients and staff while minimizing disruptions to healthcare services. Construction barriers, access routes, temporary utility requirements, dust control measures, and shutdown coordination shall be incorporated into the project design and execution. The completed project shall provide modernized and reliable facility infrastructure that supports ongoing clinical operations, improves building performance, addresses life safety and code compliance requirements, mitigates water intrusion and building envelope deficiencies, and enhances telecommunications, security, and fire protection systems throughout the facility. All completed work shall be fully commissioned, tested, and integrated with existing VA systems and infrastructure in accordance with applicable VA standards and requirements. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-build approach outlined in Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) 36-101-2, Use of two-phase design-build selection procedures. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. The Government anticipates advertising this project in the timeframe of late December 2026 to early January 2027. The VAPM Magnitude of Construction for this project is between $20,000.000.00 and $50,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 236220 applies to this procurement. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 740 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all design and construction related services. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, DUNS number and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a statement of interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. *Please ensure that the individual bonding capacity is in line with the VAPM Magnitude of Construction listed above. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. title: Jacksonville Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Enterprise Dredge Delivery Center (EDDC) requires a contract to provide maintenance dredging for Jacksonville Harbor. Jacksonville Harbor: The Jacksonville Harbor, FL - FY27 O and M Contract (non-fed sponsor Jacksonville Port Authority (JAXPORT)) for maintenance dredging typically requires hopper and pipeline/mechanical dredge(s) depending on work location in the~ 20-mile federal channel. The dredge(s) must have the capability to dredge maintenance material up to a depth of -47 ft MLLW (w/additional depths for required advanced maintenance areas and allowable over depths) and to transport the dredged sediment to both a designated Dredged Material Placement Area (DMPA) known as Bartram Island and the Ocean Dredge Material Disposal Site (ODMDS) located approximately 6 nautical miles offshore. Dredged material shall be placed upland in Bartram Island Cell F and the Jacksonville ODMDS Release Zone C1 depending on the specific reach to be dredged. The transport distance to the designated placement areas varies significantly, ranging from direct, local placement to a few miles for the upland placement area and up to 6 miles for ocean disposal from the tip of the south jetty. The work is divided into a base and five options. The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within ten (10) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use not later than 220 days after the Contractor receives the notice to proceed. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. Base: 120 calendar days. Option A: 15 calendar days. Option B: 20 calendar days. Option C: 30 calendar days. title: Construction Services for Confined Aquatic Disposal Cell Construction and Maintenance Dredging of the Providence River Federal Navigation Project, Providence, Rhode Island.
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing a Sources Sought Announcement for the upcoming dredging project located in Providence, Rhode Island. This announcement is to determine the interest, availability and capability of Small and Large Business concerns as described below. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990. The solicitation for this project is anticipated to be issued on or about 15 March 2027. The construction will begin in September 2027 and is expected to take approximately 2 years to complete. The estimated construction cost is between $80,000,000 and $100,000,000. The Providence River Maintenance Dredging project involves two major sequences of dredging and disposal activities. The first work sequence will be the construction of a new Confined Aquatic Disposal (CAD) cell adjacent to the Providence River. The second work sequence under this contract will include maintenance dredging of the Providence River and Harbor Federal Navigation Project (FNP) to its authorized depths and dimensions. The proposed work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 5,500,000 cubic yards (cy) of material using closed clamshell buckets for both major sequences of work over the course of two years. The new CAD cell will be in the Edgewood Basin area located adjacent to the Providence FNP (hereafter the �Edgewood Shoals North (ESN) CAD cell�). To access the CAD cell area, an access channel will be dug between the Providence FNP and the CAD cell area. The access channel will be approximately 100 ft wide and -25 MLLW deep. The CAD cell will have surface dimensions of approximately 1000 ft. by 1000 ft. and be dug to a depth of -60 MLLW. The material excavated to build the access channel is generally a mix of sandy silt and shell fragments. Within the CAD cell area the material is generally described as soft grey to black organic silt with some layers of firm sandy silt and some shell fragments and coarse-grained material. Material excavated from the access channel and CAD cell area will be placed at four locations: Port Edgewood Basin, the Fox Point Reach CAD cells, Prudence Island Disposal Site, and the Rhode Island Sound Disposal Site. This work consists of mechanically dredging approximately 3,200,000 cy to construct thew ESN CAD cell and its access channel, which must be completed before maintenance dredging of the FNP can begin. The maintenance dredging proposed work consists of mechanically dredging the Providence River FNP to the full -40 MLLW depth plus 2-feet of allowable overdepth. 2,300,000 cy (1,200,000 cy required depth, with up to 1,100,000 cy overdepth) of shoaled material consisting generally of poorly graded medium to fine sand with silt. The dredge material from this maintenance portion of work will be placed in the ESN CAD cell. Environmental coordination and permitting is being completed by the U.S. Army of Engineers, New England District. All dredging and disposal activities for this project have prescribed work windows that incorporate environmental and recreational time of year restrictions. Refer to the Draft Specification Section provided with this announcement for specifics on the time of year work restrictions. In order to accomplish all dredging requirements within the specified dredging window it is expected that the Contractor will need to meet a production rate of 300,000 CY per 30 calendar days. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is requesting responses to the questions below from both small and large businesses[MC1] . Draft drawings showing a concept design plan and draft Specification Section of 01 11 00 SUMMARY OF WORK have been provided with this announcement to help provide more context for the contract work and responses to these questions. Considering the different disposal locations, are there suggestions on a bid structure that will provide for the most accurate costs of different disposal locations? Any draft restrictions that may impact dredging and/or disposal operations? Any concerns on the period of performance of September 2027 to September 2029 considering the environmental windows and amount of work? If so, why? Any comments about the bed leveling planned in the Fox Point Reach? Are there concerns about this part of the plan, if so, why? Interested firms should also demonstrate their project experience, by providing two (2) projects within the last ten years, which meet the following requirements: Dredging by mechanical means demonstrating a minimum production rate of 300,000 cubic yards in one consecutive 30-day period. Experience with placement of dredged material at an open water placement site in New England during the fall/winter months of October through March. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, etc.), type of equipment the firm is proposing to use on the project, and two (2) example projects performed by the firm in the last ten (10) years (including Points of Contact for those projects) showing experience with the proposed equipment at the production rate listed above. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications meeting the same qualifications listed above, which will be used to support the bidder's effort. Firms may use subcontractor experience to demonstrate experience with the requirements, but the role and work performed by each team member (prime and subcontractors) on projects demonstrating that team member's experience shall be the same as the role for that team member for this project. Bid bond will need to be provided with the bid. Responses are limited to twenty pages and due by December 03 , 2026. Responses should be addressed to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District, 696 Virginia Road, Concord, MA 01742-2751, ATTN: Kyle Hall, or electronically to Kyle.K.Hall@usace.army.mil. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) for CNC Machine Repair, Parts, Programming, and Training Services Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD)
description: The Blue Grass Army Depot, CCRI-MII-B Depot Support Branch/Munitions and Industrial Base Directorate Army Contracting Command - Rock Island intends to establish a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) under the modernized authority of the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO), specifically leveraging RFO 12.201-1(e)(3) and Class Deviation RFO-2025-16. The BPA will facilitate the streamlined, repetitive procurement of services and repair parts to perform diagnostic troubleshooting, emergency and routine repairs, preventative maintenance, software programming, and operator/programmer training for covered systems that include: CNC Machinery: HAAS Mini Mill, HAAS VF6, HAAS SL10, Doosan Puma 2600SY. Robotic Motion Systems & Controllers: FANUC Robots (M-20iA, R-2000iB); FANUC Controllers (M-20iA, R-30iA). Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs): Allen-Bradley, Mitsubishi, Siemens (all variants utilizing industrial ladder/logic software). This combined synopsis and solicitation serves as the official public notice of the Government's intent to establish a BPA. The primary objective is to create a flexible �charge account� with a qualified, responsible source to fulfill anticipated repetitive needs efficiently. This requirement utilizes the North American Industry Classification System Code (NAICS) 811310 Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance with a size standard of $12.5 Million. This BPA shall not obligate any funds. A BPA is not a Contract. In accordance with FAR 12.201-1-3(e)(3)(iv)(B), the Government is obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases made via properly executed BPA Call Orders made under the BPA. The BPA Master Limit is $750,000. No single BPA Call Order shall exceed $250,000 in total cost. Please note, there is no guarantee that any or all requirements for the services described herein will be issued using an established BPA. The full details and applicable provisions and clauses are available in the attachments of this notice.

title: PIGA Float Assembly Repair Program
description: Login at https://piee.eb.mil and search for 'FA821426RB002' to obtain more details.* Documents related to this procurment are only available through PIEE. 1. Executive Summary: Background & Objective The U.S. Air Force has a critical requirement to support the Minuteman III (MMIII) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM) by maintaining the operational readiness of the Missile Guidance Set (MGS) to meet warfighter requirements. Specifically, this effort supports the repair line for the Pendulous Integrated Gyroscopic Accelerometer (PIGA) Float Assembly. The PIGA Float is a critical and precise sub-assembly that serves as the heart of the PIGA instrument, enabling it to measure missile acceleration. Each MGS contains three separate PIGA instruments (each housing a PIGA Float). Without this critical component, the ICBM would cease to function properly. The PIGA Float repair effort is a continuous operation necessary to avoid mission degradation. Quality control and precision engineering are paramount due to the strategic importance of the MMIII weapon system. The contractor must maintain stringent quality assurance protocols to guarantee that each repaired PIGA Float meets the rigorous military specifications. 2. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide the necessary personnel, facilities, and expertise to support the PIGA Float Assembly repair line. The primary scope includes: Repair Operations - The re-manufacture, rebuild, and repair of PIGA Float Assemblies. Volume / Throughput - The repair of 96 PIGA Floats per year. Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) - The repair and/or replacement of GFE as required to support continuous operation of the PIGA Float repair line 3. Contract Structure & Period of Performance The Government anticipates awarding an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract utilizing a mix of Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) and Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) pricing arrangements. Contract Duration - 5-Year IDIQ Anticipated Ordering Period - 1 November 2026 � 31 October 2031 Task Order Structure - Annual issuance of new, two-year non-severable Task Orders 4. Acquisition Authority & Strategy In accordance with Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 5.1, this solicitation is an intended sole-source procurement. The Government will solicit and negotiate with only one source: Honeywell Aerospace (CAGE: 09128). This action is taken under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by RFO 6.103-1. Market research�including Sources Sought Synopsis FA821425CBPIGA (posted 29 May 2025)�concluded that Honeywell Aerospace is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling the Government�s requirement without causing unacceptable delays to the MMIII weapon system mission. Note: While this is not a request for competitive proposals, information received from other responsible sources identifying their interest and capability will be considered solely to determine whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future, at the Government�s discretion. 5. Proposal Submission Instructions All proposals submitted in response to this solicitation must be submitted electronically through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. No other methods of proposal submission (e.g., email, hard copy, DoD SAFE) will be accepted. Offerors must be registered in PIEE and have the appropriate roles activated to submit proposals via the Solicitation module prior to the proposal due date. Mandatory Pricing Rubric: Submission of the attached Pricing Rubric is a mandatory requirement. Proposals submitted without a completed Pricing Rubric will be automatically rejected by the PIEE solicitation module and will not be considered for evaluation. Submission Cutoff: Proposals will not be accepted after the solicitation closes. Timely submission is the sole responsibility of the offeror, and late proposals will not be evaluated unless otherwise stated under RFO guidelines.

title: DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) PHASE III GROUNDWATER TREATMENT PLANT CONSTRUCTION, NWIRP BETHPAGE, WANTAGH, NEW YORK
description: Solicitation Number: N4008527R0048 This notice does NOT constitute a request for proposal, request for quote, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to make notice of a proposed contract action for performing construction services for Design-Bid-Build (DBB) Phase III Groundwater Treatment Plant Construction, Naval Weapons Industrial Reserve Plant (NWIRP) Bethpage, Wantagh, New York. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: This Design-Bid-Build project aims to address a plume of contaminated groundwater that has spread south from the former NWIRP and Northrop Grumman properties. This contamination, primarily consisting of chlorinated VOCs (like TCE) and 1,4-dioxane, is being remediated as required by the Navy and the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation. The core of this phase is the construction of a new Groundwater Treatment Plant (GWTP) designed to intercept the leading edge of the plume. The plant will treat the captured water to meet drinking water standards using a process that includes sand filters, an Advanced Oxidation Process (AOP), and Granular Activated Carbon (GAC). The scope of work involves the complete construction and commissioning of the facility. This includes completing three groundwater recovery wells and the associated underground piping to bring contaminated water to the plant. The facility itself will house numerous systems, including large storage tanks, multiple filter types, the AOP system, and granular activated carbon units. The project also covers the construction of two new buildings for the treatment plant and offices, along with all necessary structural, electrical, and plumbing infrastructure. The work includes: buried piping systems, pavements, and miscellaneous items; one underground vault; piping, valves, fittings for three recovery wells and wiring, instruments, and equipment within the conduit, manholes, and vaults; three Reinforced Plastic (FRP) vertical storage tanks; one glass fused Backwash waste steel tank; three Multimedia Vertical Pressure Filters (MMF) unit vessels, two Horizontal Cartridge Filters, one Ozone-Hydrogen Peroxide Advance Oxidation Process (AOP) system; three Liquid Phase Granular Activated Carbon (LGAC) unit vessels; eight pumps with piping, valves, supports and appurtenances; two blowers; chemical feed systems for Sodium Hydroxide, Sodium Hypochlorite and Hydrogen Peroxide; two buildings (treatment plant and office), foundations, and interior/exterior concrete slabs on grade and under-slab utility coordination; structural and architectural roof and systems; one 1200A, 277/480V, 3-phase, 3-Wire Service; an MCC for motor VFDs; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC); a PLC and SCADA system, and internet/cellular gateway to enable off- site Phase III System process parameters; earthwork, including pad excavation and site re-grading; site utilities; fencing; and a fire protection system. The completion time for this contract is 1,095 calendar days after award. This solicitation is being advertised as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. This source selection procurement requires both non-price (technical and past performance) and price proposals and will utilize the best value continuum process at FAR 15.103-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0048, Rev 1), Tradeoff approach. The basis for evaluation and evaluation factors for award will be included in the solicitation. Large business concerns are required to submit a subcontracting plan prior to award of the contract. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this project is 237110, Water and Sewer Line and Related Structures Construction, with a small business size standard of $45,000,000. The magnitude of construction for this project is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. The anticipated award of this contract is March 2027. An SBA Small Business Search (SBS) and a Sources Sought Notice was conducted and issued on 21 January 2026, seeking eligible Small Businesses, HUBZone Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Businesses, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses, and Women-Owned Small Businesses to determine the opportunity for a set-aside. The Government invited prospective offerors with the capabilities of performing construction services that meet or exceed the stated requirement to submit a capabilities statement. Respondents were required to submit relevant experience in performing efforts of similar size, scope, and complexity within the last seven (7) years. Based on the market research conducted for this procurement and in accordance with FAR 19.104-1 (DPCAP CD 2026-O0037, Rev 1), the Contracting Officer has determined that there is not a reasonable expectation that an adequate number of Small Business firms would respond to or be qualified to perform the requirements of this solicitation. Successful award and completion of the requirements can be achieved by soliciting the contract as "Unrestricted" for full and open competition. A DD2579 Small Business Coordination Record was approved by the NAVFAC MIDLANT Small Business Professional on 30 March 2026. On 02 April 2026, the Small Business Administration (SBA) Procurement Center Representative (PCR) concurred with this recommendation. The Request for Proposal (RFP) will be issued by NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic CON22 on or about 03 December 2026. The solicitation number will be N4008527R0048. All documents will be in Adobe PDF file format and downloadable from the PIEE and Sam.gov website. The official address to the solicitation is https://piee.eb.mil and https://www.sam.gov. Contractors are encouraged to register for the solicitation when downloading from the website. Only registered contractors will be notified by email when amendments to the solicitation are issued. A free Acrobat Reader, required to view the PDF files, can be downloaded from the Adobe website. IMPORTANT NOTICE: All prospective offerors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM). You must have an active registration in SAM to do business with the federal government. For additional information, go to https://www.sam.gov. Questions or comments regarding this notice may be addressed by email to shayna.t.eichner.civ@us.navy.mil

title: Sonic Boom Launch Noise Analysis RFI _NAICS 541330, 541715
description: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a solicitation or a request for proposals (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm's ability to submit a proposal should a formal solicitation be issued in the future. Facilities and infrastructure at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (CCSFS) are exposed to intense acoustic loads and sonic booms from an increasing cadence of launch operations. Existing historical data is primarily based on aircraft overflights and has limited applicability to the unique pressure signatures generated by modern launch vehicles (including Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Starship/Super Heavy, Vulcan, New Glenn, and other current or proposed vehicles). The Government requires development of a scientifically defensible material testing methodology and a predictive engineering model to evaluate the effects of launch noise and sonic booms on both current and legacy construction materials, infrastructure, and facility types at CCSFS. The effort shall support informed decisions on facility sustainment, retrofitting, or replacement. Reference the attached Statement of Objective for a more detailed description of this requirement. Please see attached RFI for further directions. Please respond to the questions found within the RFI document if interested no later than 3 December 2026, 2:00 PM EST. You may address questions in a narrative, annotated outline, bullet or table format. Thank you!

description: DESCRIPTION: This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice for project number 596A4-27-101 that requires Architect/Engineering (A/E) Design Services to Upgrade Fire Alarm System at the Lexington VA Healthcare System, Troy Bowling Campus. THIS ANNOUNCEMENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. ONLY THE A/E FIRMS RESPONDING TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT BY SUBMITTING AN SF330 PACKAGE ON TIME WILL BE CONSIDERED FOR INITIAL EVALUATION. FOLLOWING INITIAL EVALUATION OF THE A/E FIRMS AND THEIR SF330S, A SOLICITATION FOR A PRICE PROPOSAL WILL BE SENT TO THE HIGHEST TECHNICALLY RATED A/E FIRM TO PROVIDE THE TYPE OF SERVICE(S) REQUIRED. The A/E Services contract that is anticipated to be awarded will be procured in accordance with the Brooks Act (Public Law 92- 582), Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 36.6 and VA Acquisition Regulation 836.6. In accordance with FAR 36.209 Construction Contracts With Architect-Engineer Firms , no contract for the construction of a project shall be awarded to the firm that designed the project or its subsidiaries or affiliates, except with the approval of the head of the agency or authorized representative. A/E DESIGN SERVICES SCOPE SYNOPSIS: The A/E will be required to perform comprehensive field investigations to base their design documents off of, this includes, above ceiling surveys that the VA will assist with access to all required spaces. Project will replace existing fire alarm system at the Troy Bowling Campus to include Building 1, Building 1A and Building 4. Replacement includes hospital space, parking garage as well as crawl space as required per code. Size of existing facility is 537,542 square feet. Existing fire alarm system is required to remain in service until new system is active and ready to be utilized. Phasing of cutover from existing to new system to be determined by A/E. Project will correct FCA Deficiencies 338139, 45058, 49003, 49909, 49035, 49963 and 49935. New fire alarm system will be required to interact with multiple systems throughout the hospital to include, but not limited to: Door magnets, elevators, HVAC systems, kitchen hood systems, sprinkler system, specialty fire suppression systems, door locking systems, smoke dampers, duct detectors and other systems. The estimated magnitude of construction for this A/E requirement is between $10,000,000 and $20,000,000. END OF DESIGN SCOPE SYNOPSIS Digital copies of the as-builts are limited. The consultant will be expected to fully investigate and confirm the validity of hard copy as-builts and other drawings. This will include independent investigation of the VAMC s flat files by the consultant to determine and procure the information required for the complete design. All offerors are advised that in accordance with VAAR 836.606-73 the total cost of the architect or engineer services contracted for must not exceed 6 percent of the estimated cost of the construction project plus any fees for related services and activities. Additionally, FAR Clause 52.236-2 (c) - Design Within Funding Limitation, will be applicable to this procurement action. Design limitation costs will be provided to the most highly rated AE firm selected to complete the design. Interested firms should submit their current SF-330 to matthew.whisman@va.gov. title: Air Force Contract Augmentation Program (AFCAP) VI
description: The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS/PKD) is issuing this solicitation for the Air Force Contract Augmentation Program VI (AFCAP VI). This is a Multiple-Award Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract designed to provide rapid, global contingency planning, logistics, and emergency construction capabilities to the Department of the Air Force, other DoD components, and Federal agencies. The AFCAP serves as a responsive, global force multiplier for commanders and Government agencies, supporting contingencies both within the contiguous United States (CONUS) and outside the contiguous United States (OCONUS).The AFCAP supports United States (U.S.) national interests and security objectives by providing rapid-response capabilities for contingency planning, deployment, training/equipping of forces, emergency/contingency construction, logistics/commodities, and services. These capabilities align with definitions in the DOD Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms. AFCAP provides a full range of Base Operating/Life Support (BOS/BLS) and logistical support on an as-required basis to support a wide spectrum of activities, including, but are not limited to: Major Theater War(s); Small Scale Contingencies; Irregular Warfare; responses to Violent Extremist Organizations (VEO); foreign assistance, developmental assistance, humanitarian assistance, and security assistance (including Foreign Military Sales); peacekeeping; counterinsurgency, counterdrug and counterterrorism operations; maritime security operations; recovery operations and denial measures; domestic/international emergency support; infrastructure/facility design/build, design/build/operate, demolition, and site restoration; deliberate and crisis action planning; and military exercises (including Joint Chiefs of Staff sponsored) authorized by the National Command Authority.

title: Mission Module Engineering and Technical Services
description: **ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR AWARD UNDER THIS SOLICITATION.*** Request for Proposal (RFP) (N6133127R0006) under the Seaport NxG Multiple Award Contract (MAC), for Mission Module Engineering and Technical Support. This effort has been previously been posted under the Opportunities page as the following: Sources Sought Notice (N6133126SNQ27), dated (Posted 7 May 2026) and the follow-up Advance Planning Notice/Pre-Solicitation Notice dated (16 June 2026). ***RESPONSES MUST BE SUBMITTED VIA THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE.*** ***ALL DOCUMENTS ARE AVAILABLE WITHIN THE PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE*** Questions and Answers WILL TAKE PLACE THROUGH PIEE MODULE AND POSTED TO PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE BY ATTACHMENT***This is a solicitation for SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ONLY. This solicitation is to provide services to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center Panama City Division (NSWC PCD) Modular Integration Division as the lead for engineering, analysis, and planning support for the modularization of off-board systems in support of the littoral warfare mission area. The requirements will include systems engineering, packaging and handling of off-board system hardware, system integration of legacy and emerging littoral mission systems, sea frame integration of mission modules, development of mission system common computing environments (e.g. Mission Package Computing Environment (MPCE)) and integrated communications networks (e.g. Multiple Vehicle Communication System(MVCS)), distributed engineering testing, and supporting the Government in validation and verification. Specifically, these requirements include the general program, engineering, technical, and integrated logistics support requirements for the Littoral Combat Ship (LCS)Mission Modules (MM) program at NSWC PCD. Access to the solicitation is through the link. Access to the attachments are in the PIEE SOLICITATION MODULE through the link.
